title: Heat map
description:
A heat map colors a grid: `x_column` across, `y_column` down, `value_column` the color.
The default style packs two rows into one line (half blocks); `renderer: block` gives
every row a line and can write the values. See `:help dbdash-chart-types`.

query.sql:
WITH RECURSIVE d(n) AS (SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT n + 1 FROM d WHERE n < 5),
h(n) AS (SELECT 8 UNION ALL SELECT n + 1 FROM h WHERE n < 18)
SELECT 'Day ' || d.n AS day, printf('%02d', h.n) AS hour,
       abs((d.n * 7 + h.n * 13) % 50) AS requests
FROM d, h

show.title: halfblock (default)
show.description:
Two rows of the grid per line (▀ with a foreground and a background color), a legend of
the scale underneath.

show.title: renderer: block, show_values, format
show.description:
`renderer: block` gives every row its own line; `show_values` writes each value in its
cell (black or white, whichever reads better), in the Python `axes.y_axis.format`.

query.sql:

show.title: color_scale, scale_min, scale_max
show.description:
Your own colors from low to high (`color_scale`, "#rrggbb" stops, ECharts
`inRange.color`) over a fixed range (`scale_min` / `scale_max`): values outside take the
end colors.

show.title: color_steps (piecewise), legend: false
show.description:
`color_steps` colors by thresholds instead of a gradient (ECharts piecewise
visualMap): a value takes the color of the highest step it reaches. `legend: false`
hides the scale.
